count.jq:92 | `||` and `|&` are taken as a pipe, because `parts` splits them into two `|` separators and an empty part (count.jq:41). The command after them then sets `.drop` back to false, so a read that went into a count or a file still counts as a trace (kept) | `cat <cache>/skills/github/filing.md | wc -l || true`, or `sed -n 1,9p …/filing.md | head -5 > /tmp/x || true`, or `cat …/filing.md |& wc -l`. Each one gives a trace of filing.md. The test has no sample with `|| …` after a pipeline. I am not sure how often real calls add `|| true` after such a pipeline.
count.jq:92 | A `$(...)` inside a later stage of a pipeline ends with sep `)`. That adds the pipe to `.reads` before the last stage decides | `cat …/filing.md | head -n "$(echo 20)" | wc -l` gives a trace of filing.md, but its output goes into `wc`. Also `cat …/filing.md | grep -c "$(echo x)"`. This is rare.
count.jq:81 | `$writes` does not see a write to a file by `&>` or `1>`: the pattern `(^|[^0-9&])>` leaves out a `>` after a digit or `&` | `cat …/github/merge.md &>/dev/null`, or `cat …/merge.md 1>/tmp/x`, gives a trace, but no line reaches the context.
count.sh:76 | A pending trace takes effect on any result row, also a failed Bash call (`is_error` true, "Exit code N"), though no line of the file was shown | `cat <cache>/<wrong-version>/skills/github/merge.md` ("No such file"), or `grep -n squash …/merge.md` with no match (exit 1). Each one counts as kept for the next merge. The check `$5 != "true"` is not there. A wrong cache path is plausible when the model guesses the version folder.
count.sh:57 | A compaction does not clear `traced`. A Read or a load before a `compact_boundary` still counts as kept for a first moment after it, though the summary removed that text from the context. The first table counts compactions for this reason | A long session reads take-in.md, compacts, and runs take-in-check.sh after it: kept. I am not sure whether Claude Code puts a loaded SKILL.md back after a compaction. A Read result does not come back.
rules.json:7 | The gh write regex marks a GraphQL read query as a write when a flag comes before `graphql`. `(?!graphql)` only acts directly after `api`, and the `-f` then matches the field alternative | `gh api --paginate graphql -f query='query { viewer { login } }'`, or `gh api -H "Accept: x" graphql -F owner=o -f query='{ … }'`, is a moment of "github before a gh write". moments.tsv has a sample only with `--paginate … mutation`.
rules.json:58 | The filing rule misses `gh api` with a flag before the endpoint, or with a quoted endpoint: `\S*repos/` cannot cross a space, and `(?=\s|$)` fails at a `"` | `gh api -X POST repos/o/r/issues --input b.json`, `gh api --method POST repos/o/r/issues -f title=x`, and `gh api "repos/o/r/issues" -f title=x` give no moment of "filing.md before a new issue". Rule 1 does see `-X POST` before the endpoint.
